**P1 — Hook/Background (~80 words):**
Vision token pruning works reliably in ViTs (DynamicViT 66% removal <0.5% loss, ToMe 40% >99%). VLAs use the same encoders with hundreds of tokens dominating LLM input. For real-time robotic control at 5-10 Hz, token reduction would speed up quadratic attention. Several works explore this (FastV, VLA-Cache, VLA-IAP). But they share an untested assumption: pruning behaves consistently across architectures.

**P2 — Gap (~60 words):**
VLAs differ in their vision connector — the module transforming ViT patches into LLM tokens. Pixel-shuffle folds patches spatially; MLP projectors map independently; linear projections pass through directly. No prior work has systematically tested how these connector designs affect pruning sensitivity in closed-loop control, where a single wrong action compounds irrecoverably.

**P3 — Discovery (~120 words):**
We conduct the first cross-architecture study of vision token pruning in 5 VLA models (450M-7B). Key findings:
- π0 (linear projection, 3.3B): offline loss IMPROVES 2.4% at 90% token removal
- X-VLA (linear + BART encoder, 880M): robust at k≥0.9 (97.6% SR), then cliff to 56.2% at k=0.7

- SmolVLA (pixel-shuffle, 450M): catastrophic collapse, 0% at 5% removal

The controlled comparison between π0 (256 tokens, linear) and OpenVLA (256 tokens, MLP) isolates the connector as causal: same token count, same encoder lineage, 63pp gap at k=0.1.

**P4 — Solution (~60 words):**
For vulnerable architectures, we propose VTR (Vision Token Re-encoder): a lightweight cross-attention module that re-encodes rather than deletes tokens. At 75% compression, VTR recovers 60.1% SR where all deletion methods yield 0%. A parameter-matched MLP adapter achieves 63.4% (p=0.15), confirming re-encoding itself is the causal factor.

**P5 — Contributions (enumerate):**
1. Architecture-dependent compressibility taxonomy: 5 models × 3 connector families. Effective pipeline complexity determines pruning tolerance. (§4)
2. CV as continuous diagnostic: token importance heterogeneity predicts degradation onset from a single forward pass. (§5.1-§5.2)
3. VTR re-encoding overcomes cliff-edge: 0% → 60%+ SR at 75% compression, architecture-independent. M-curve flat: M=16 ≈ M=128. (§4.5, §5.3)
4. Offline metric disconnect: standard offline proxies underestimate closed-loop failure severity. (§5.4)
